- When sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast, especially in early horizon; reduce peak forecasts by 5–15% if sentiment > 0.7 for 3+ days.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >15% above recent mean) followed by true outcome drop, apply “overshoot correction” — reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (negative) and model forecasts are rising, apply “mean reversion bias” — cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7-day average if sentiment < -0.7.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., >10% gap for 3+ days), apply “lag correction” — shift forecast down by 2–5% for next 5 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days if sentiment drops below 0.3.
- Avoid forecasting above 1.2x recent 14-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.8) and no major event is pending — otherwise, cap at 1.1x to avoid over-optimism.
